sections.title: Segments
sections.subtitle: Only disclosed for FY2025 and FY2026 under the current five-segment structure

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentEbit.title: Segment EBIT
segmentEbit.content:
BlueScope reports five segments: Australian Steel Products, North Star BlueScope (US electric-arc-furnace mill), New Zealand & Pacific Steel, Building Products Asia/NA and Coated Products Americas.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: North Star has grown from a minority contributor into the largest single segment by EBIT in FY2026 (A$805.3m of A$1,192.3m group underlying-style EBIT), so the group result now leans heavily on US electric-arc-furnace steel spreads and the USD/AUD rate, not the legacy Australian mill. Only FY2025 and FY2026 are shown -- BlueScope's segment structure and disclosure changed and a longer comparable series isn't available.

What to watch:

  • North Star's share of group EBIT rising further (more US-cycle and FX exposure)
  • Australian Steel Products EBIT relative to domestic construction/manufacturing demand
  • Any one segment's swing dominating the year-on-year group change

despatches.title: Despatch volumes
despatches.content:
Despatches are tonnes of steel product shipped out of each segment (in kilotonnes, kt) -- BlueScope's own throughput measure, separate from the dollar revenue line.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: comparing despatch growth against segment EBIT growth separates volume from price/spread -- North Star's FY2026 EBIT jump came with despatches up only modestly (2,881.8kt to 2,976.5kt), so the earnings gain was mostly a wider steel spread, not more tonnes sold. New Zealand & Pacific Steel does not disclose a comparable despatch figure and is omitted here. Only FY2025/FY2026 are available.

What to watch:

  • Despatch volumes flat or falling while EBIT rises (a spread/price story that can reverse)
  • Coated Products Americas and Building Products Asia/NA volumes as a read on US/Asian construction demand

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For BlueScope Steel Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
